svg.title: What TSA's pages say about shoes and large electronics at the checkpoint: standard screening, CT equipment, TSA PreCheck, the July 2025 shoes release, the officer's instructions and page dates.
svg.text: TSA: shoes and laptops
What TSA's pages say
Standard screening
Laptops and other electronics larger
than a cell phone: take them out of
the bag and put them in a bin.
(Travel Checklist; Security Screening
page.) The checklist lists no shoe step.
Where CT equipment is used
CT page: under current procedures,
laptops may stay in the bag.
Juneau release (local, July 13, 2026):
at Juneau's new CT scanners, laptops
and other electronics may stay in the
bag, 3-1-1 liquids need not come out,
and all carry-on items go in a bin.
TSA PreCheck
Laptops page: PreCheck travelers do not
need to remove shoes, laptops, 3-1-1
liquids, belts or light jackets. Two other
pages say the same about shoes. These
describe PreCheck; they are not a stated
shoe rule for other passengers.
Shoes: July 2025 release
Passengers at domestic airports can keep
their shoes on; other security layers
still apply. The PreCheck pages above do
not mention the release, and TSA does not
say how the two fit together.
On the day
Security Screening page: listen to the
instructions of the TSA officer. The pages
do not say how CT equipment and PreCheck
combine at a checkpoint.
Page dates
Release: July 8, 2025. Laptops page:
July 15, 2026. Tablets page: July 21, 2026.
Steel Toe Boots page: May 26, 2022.
Checklist, CT and Security Screening
pages: no date.
Sources: eight TSA pages; read Nov. 9, 2026
